questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The rider plans to turn left.
The rider is about to stop.
The rider plans to turn right.
The rider is about to slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: The rider plans to turn left.
questions.explanation: Riders use hand signals instead of turn signals. When a rider extends their left arm straight out to the side, it means they plan to turn left or change lanes to the left.

questions.question: What may help if your drive chain is slipping?
questions.explanation: If your chain is slipping, tightening it may fix the problem. If tightening does not work, replace the chain before riding again.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, what should you do to adjust for their weight?

options.text: Keep a shorter distance behind other vehicles than you would alone.
Brake later than you would if riding alone.

questions.explanation: A passenger adds weight. Your motorcycle will need more time to speed up, slow down, and turn. Reduce your speed, start slowing earlier, increase your following distance, and look for larger gaps when turning or merging with traffic.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle, what should you do?

options.text: Complete the pass without exceeding the speed limit.
You can finish the pass in a no passing zone if you started it before the zone began.
You may exceed the speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Complete the pass without exceeding the speed limit.
questions.explanation: All passes must stay within the posted speed limit and only happen in areas where passing is allowed.

questions.question: When slowing or stopping, when should you use both brakes?

options.text: Only when the pavement is wet.
Only when riding in the city.

questions.explanation: Using both the front and rear brakes gives you the best stopping power. Use both brakes every time you slow down or stop.

questions.question: When should a motorcyclist shift gears?

options.text: By changing power suddenly in a turn.
While riding the brake through a turn.

questions.explanation: Shift gears before you enter a turn.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a slippery surface?
questions.explanation: Many surfaces can be hazardous. Wet pavement, loose gravel, sand, mud, snow, ice, painted lane markings, and metal covers are all more slippery than dry pavement.

questions.question: Which colors make riders most visible?
questions.explanation: Wear bright orange, red, yellow, or green clothing to help others see you.

questions.question: What do goggles protect?

options.text: Your face but not your eyes.
Your eyes, but not your face.
Neither your face nor your eyes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your eyes, but not your face.
questions.explanation: Goggles protect your eyes only. Only a face shield can protect your entire face in a crash.

questions.question: If you shift to a lower gear while riding too fast, what could happen?

options.text: Your motorcycle may jerk and the rear tire may skid.
Your motorcycle may jerk and the front tire may skid.
Your motorcycle may jerk and a warning light will appear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your motorcycle may jerk and the rear tire may skid.
questions.explanation: If you shift to a lower gear while riding too fast, your motorcycle may jerk and the rear tire may skid, causing you to lose control. Always slow down enough before shifting to a lower gear.

questions.question: When a group of riders passes another vehicle, what should they do?

options.text: One rider should finish passing before the next rider begins.
Several riders should pass at the same time.
The last rider should wave to signal no more motorcycles are coming.

questions.correctAnswerText: One rider should finish passing before the next rider begins.
questions.explanation: Riders in a group should pass one at a time. Each rider must complete their pass and return to the group before the next rider passes.

questions.question: In a normal turn, how should the motorcycle and rider lean?

options.text: They should lean together at the same angle.
They should lean in opposite directions.
The motorcycle leans, but the rider stays upright.
The rider leans, but the motorcycle stays upright.

questions.correctAnswerText: They should lean together at the same angle.
questions.explanation: In normal turns, the motorcycle and rider lean together at the same angle. In slow, tight turns, only the motorcycle leans while the rider stays upright.

questions.question: What does a proper lane position NOT do?

options.text: Help you see and be seen better.

questions.explanation: A good lane position helps you see and be seen, avoid hazards and blind spots, and communicate your plans to others. It does not help you avoid traffic signals.

questions.question: What does a plastic, shatter-resistant face shield do?

options.text: It is not necessary if you have a windshield.
It does not protect as well as goggles.

questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your whole face in a crash. Goggles only protect your eyes. A windshield does not replace a face shield or goggles.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They tell drivers about upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: When approaching a blind intersection, what should you do?

options.text: Ride in the part of your lane where other drivers will see you as early as possible.
Always stay in the left lane to be farthest from oncoming traffic.
Slowly creep up to the intersection.
Weave slightly in your lane so your headlight is more visible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the part of your lane where other drivers will see you as early as possible.
questions.explanation: Move to the part of your lane where oncoming drivers will see you earliest. For example, if turning right, ride in the left part of your lane instead of the center.

questions.question: After drinking alcohol, what reduces its effects?
questions.explanation: Your liver removes alcohol at a fixed rate. Nothing speeds this up. Only time will reduce alcohol's effects.

questions.question: What is true about brightly-colored helmets?

options.text: They may help others see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: They may help others see you.
questions.explanation: A bright helmet is recommended. It protects you in a crash and helps other drivers see you on the road.

questions.question: When braking, what should you do?

options.text: Use only one brake in non-emergency situations.
Only use both brakes on wet pavement.

questions.explanation: Always use both brakes when you slow down or stop.

questions.question: Which type of sign is rectangular?
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs like speed limits are rectangular with white background and black lettering. You must follow the rules shown on these signs.

questions.question: How many alcoholic drinks can affect a rider's ability to ride?
questions.explanation: Even one drink can affect your ability to ride safely. Riding under the influence of alcohol is illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: If a tire goes flat while riding, what should you do?

options.text: Relax your grip on the handlebars.
Shift your weight toward the good tire.
Brake on the good tire and steer to the roadside.
Use both brakes and stop quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake on the good tire and steer to the roadside.
questions.explanation: Hold the handlebars firmly and ease off the throttle. Keep going straight. If you must brake, gradually use only the brake on the tire that is not flat. As you slow down, move to the side of the road, squeeze the clutch, and stop.

questions.question: The gearshift lever is operated by:
questions.explanation: The gearshift lever is in front of the left footrest. You operate it with your left foot.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, you should:
questions.explanation: With a passenger, your motorcycle sits lower and weighs more. Ride slower, especially in curves and over bumps. The extra weight means it takes longer to speed up, slow down, and stop. Keep more space between you and other vehicles.

questions.question: Your lane position should not:

options.text: Increase your ability to see and be seen.
Invite other drivers to share your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Invite other drivers to share your lane.
questions.explanation: Choose your lane position to avoid blind spots, improve visibility, avoid hazards, and provide an escape route. Position yourself to prevent other drivers from trying to share your lane.
